A.explanation: A frequency of $5.0 \times 10^5 \text{ Hz}$ gives a wavelength of about $600 \text{ m}$, which is in the radio wave region, not visible light.

B.explanation: A frequency of $5.0 \times 10^8 \text{ Hz}$ gives a wavelength of about $0.6 \text{ m}$, which is in the radio / UHF region, not visible light.

C.explanation: A frequency of $5.0 \times 10^{11} \text{ Hz}$ gives a wavelength of about $0.6 \text{ mm}$, which is in the microwave / infrared region, not visible light.

D.explanation: A frequency of $5.0 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ gives a wavelength of about $600 \text{ nm}$, which lies inside the $400-700 \text{ nm}$ visible range.

hints: Notice the light is visible and in a vacuum, so its speed is $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and its wavelength must be around $400-700 \text{ nm}$.
Connect speed, frequency and wavelength with $c = f\lambda$, so visible light must have $f = c/\lambda$ of order $10^{14} \text{ Hz}$.
Check each given frequency by estimating $\lambda = c/f$ - only one value gives $\lambda$ in nanometres rather than metres, millimetres or larger.
walkthrough: Identify the physics: all electromagnetic waves in a vacuum travel at $c = 3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and visible light is defined by wavelength $\lambda$ roughly $4.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $7.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$.
State the governing relation $c = f\lambda$, rearranged to $f = c/\lambda$ for the frequency.
Substitute a typical visible wavelength, for example $\lambda = 6.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$: $f = (3.0 \times 10^8 \text{ m s}^{-1})/(6.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}) = 5.0 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$.

Compare orders of magnitude: $10^5 \text{ Hz}$, $10^8 \text{ Hz}$ and $10^{11} \text{ Hz}$ give $\lambda = 600 \text{ m}$, $0.6 \text{ m}$ and $0.6 \text{ mm}$ respectively, all far too large for visible light.
Only $5.0 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ matches the calculated visible frequency. This is option D.
